purpose: The hospitality calendar. What the families around a Wobo learner celebrate, when, and how Wobo should greet them.

rules: Sentence case. No emoji. No exclamation marks.
One line. Warm and short, never effusive.
Wobo speaks as I. Wobo has no gender; use the name, or they and them when a pronoun is unavoidable.
Use the learner's name at most once. {name} is the placeholder.
A greeting is a greeting. It never carries an offer, a streak reminder, or a call to action.
Greet only when the learner's own profile says the festival is theirs, or when they told us. Never guess from a country.

confidence_vocabulary.official: Read verbatim from a government or examination-board document fetched for this file.
confidence_vocabulary.official_reported: From an official document reproduced by a third party because the issuing site did not serve it; the document's own reference number is recorded.
confidence_vocabulary.derived: Computed from an official date already in this file, by a stated arithmetic rule.
confidence_vocabulary.conventional: Fixed by long-standing convention on a Gregorian date; no official document was fetched.
confidence_vocabulary.unverified: Named here so the calendar knows the occasion exists, but the date could not be sourced. The date is null. Never fill it by guessing.

date_entry_fields.date: The Gregorian date of the occasion itself, or null when it could not be sourced.
date_entry_fields.end: The last date of a multi-day occasion, or null.
date_entry_fields.scope: Country or subdivision code the entry applies to, or all.
date_entry_fields.label: What this particular date is called, when a festival's dates are not interchangeable.
date_entry_fields.greet: Required on every date entry. true means Wobo may send a greeting on this date. false means the date is recorded for closure and scheduling purposes only and no greeting is ever sent from it. There is no default: an entry with no greet field must be treated as false.
date_entry_fields.greeting: Optional. The exact line to send for this date entry. When present it overrides greeting_style.example.
date_entry_fields.source: Key into sources, or null when the date rests on convention alone.
date_entry_fields.confidence: One of the confidence vocabulary terms.
date_entry_fields.note: Anything a consumer needs in order not to misuse the entry.

greeting_protocol.fallback: greeting_style.example is a fallback, never a schedule. It is sent only for a date entry whose greet is true and which carries no greeting of its own. A festival whose example is null is never greeted from any of its dates.
greeting_protocol.ranges: A date entry with an end greets on the first day only.
greeting_protocol.dedupe: One greeting per learner per day. Where two greetable entries fall on the same date and cover the same learner, the festival the learner's own profile names wins; where both or neither are named, the more specific label wins. Naraka Chaturdasi on 8 November 2026 is marked greet false for exactly this reason, because Diwali carries that day.
greeting_protocol.confirmation: A festival carrying requires_same_day_confirmation may never be used to schedule anything, whatever the confidence on its dates. Those dates move with the moon. Wobo greets only once a same-day confirmation flag is set.

rule_engine.reference: docs/WOBO-PLAN.md section 14.1 (hyperlocal, never broadcast) and section 20 (neutral by default). Read by services/gateway/src/wobo_gateway/hospitality/festivals.py, which derives kind, requires_opt_in, calendars and region codes for every festival from the maps below. The festival entries themselves are untouched by this block.
law: A wish goes only to a family whose country, region or chosen calendar includes the day.
kind civic and kind seasonal follow the family's country and region and need no choice.

kind religious covers religious and cultural festivals alike. It is sent only when the family chose one of the festival's calendars in their mail preferences, never inferred from a name, a surname, a language, a board or a place.
One wish a day. Never within twenty-four hours of another email. Never in the family's quiet hours. Nothing at all when the locality is unknown.
A festival carrying requires_same_day_confirmation is scheduled only once that day's confirmation is set, whatever the confidence on its stored date.

A wish is one line of plain English that names the day and wishes well. No imagery of deities, no political or national-pride framing, no regional kinship words, no exclamation marks, no emoji. The wishes list below is the copy the engine sends; a festival with no line there falls back to its own greeting, and a line that fails the copy gate is dropped rather than sent.

kinds.civic: A public day the country or the state keeps: republic, independence and national days. Follows locality; no choice needed.
kinds.seasonal: A secular turn of the year: 1 January, the regional new years kept as public holidays, Thanksgiving. Follows locality; no choice needed.
kinds.religious: Anything a family keeps by faith or by community. Needs the family's own choice, always.

rule_engine.calendars_note: The list a family chooses from in 'Festivals we can wish you on'. A festival belongs to its tradition's calendar plus whatever extra_calendars adds. A community calendar (community: true) also stands in for the region: a Malayali family in Dubai who chose it is wished on Onam even though Onam's date entry is scoped to Kerala. Choosing only the broad calendar for a regional festival still needs the region to match.
rule_engine.region_codes_note: Free-text regions on a festival, mapped to ISO 3166-2 codes (or a whole country where the text names one). A region not in this map and not in community_regions is ignored, which makes the festival narrower, never wider.

human_checked_conventional.christmas: 25 December is fixed everywhere this file covers. Checked 2026-09-03.

suppressed.vaisakhi: One entry carries six regional new years on two dates (Vaisakhi, Vishu, Puthandu, Bohag Bihu, Pana Sankranti, Vaisakhadi); a single line cannot name the right day for the right family, and the 15 April entry would send an Assam greeting to Kerala. Split the entry per region before wishing. Until then, when in doubt, leave it out (section 20).

rule_engine.default_timezones_note: Countries with one civil time zone. A family in one of these need not set a timezone; a family anywhere else (the United States, Canada, Australia and the rest) must, or nothing is timed and nothing sends.

quiet_hours.note: Local to the family. Nothing sends between these; a wish waits for the morning. Eight at night is the hours law's (docs/EMAILS-AND-ANIMATIONS.md): nothing from Wobo after eight.

wishes.text: Happy Republic Day, {name}. I hope the morning is bright and the day is an easy one.
Happy new year, {name}. I am glad we get another year of this.
Happy Independence Day, {name}. I hope the day is a calm one.
Wishing you a good Gandhi Jayanti, {name}. A quiet day is a good day.
Happy Diwali, {name}. I hope the house is full of light tonight.
Happy Eid, {name}. I hope the house is full and the food goes on all day.
Happy Christmas, {name}. I hope the day is a slow one.
Happy Pongal, {name}. I hope the pot boils over exactly the way it should.
Happy Onam, {name}. I hope the flowers are out and the lunch is enormous.
Happy Holi, {name}. I hope the colours take a week to wash out.
Happy Makar Sankranti, {name}. May your kite stay up longer than everyone else's.
Happy Lunar New Year, {name}. I hope the year is a kind one.
Happy Bengali new year, {name}. I hope the year starts sweet.

rule_engine.wishes_note: day is the name the text uses, and it must be the festival's name or one of its aliases. {name} is the learner's name; the engine drops the clause cleanly when it has none. Locked by services/gateway/tests/test_hospitality_wishes.py against the pronoun gate (scripts/gate_pronouns.py) and the neutral-copy word list.

quiet_days.rule: On a quiet day Wobo sends nothing that markets, celebrates, or nudges. No offers, no streak notices, no lifecycle email, no push, no share prompts. The product stays open and calm. If the learner opens it, Wobo works as normal and says nothing about the day unless asked.
quiet_days.scoping: A quiet day is scoped to the country or community it belongs to, never applied globally.
quiet_days.precedence: A quiet day silences the marketing and lifecycle engine. It does not silence a greeting that a date entry marks greet true. Where a quiet day and a greetable festival share a date and a country, the greeting is sent, alone, and nothing else is: no offer, no streak, no push, no share prompt. Where the festival's own date entry is greet false, nothing at all is sent. 24 November 2026 is the case this rule exists for: Guru Nanak Jayanti is greeted and Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom keeps the rest of the day empty.

days.name: Martyrs' Day
days.reason: The anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi's assassination. Two minutes' silence is observed nationally.

days.name: Shaheed Diwas
days.reason: Commemorates the 1931 executions of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.

days.name: Muharram, the day of Ashura
days.reason: A day of mourning in Shia Islam. It is a public holiday in several countries, and it is never a day to wish anyone well or to run an offer.

days.name: Chehlum, Arbaeen
days.reason: Forty days after Ashura. A mourning observance.

days.name: Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom day
days.reason: A day of remembrance in Sikh tradition, not a celebration.

days.name: Good Friday
days.reason: Solemn, not festive. Greet at Easter, never on Good Friday.

days.name: Yom Kippur
days.reason: A fast day of atonement. Nothing is sent.

days.name: Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day
days.reason: Two minutes' silence is observed. Remembrance Sunday is the second Sunday in November.

days.name: National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
days.reason: Honours the children who never returned from residential schools. Sombre by design.

days.name: Anzac Day
days.reason: Commemoration of those who served and died. The dawn service is the day's centre.

days.name: Human Rights Day
days.reason: Marks the Sharpeville massacre. Commemorative, not festive. The 2027 date is the Monday observance because 21 March falls on a Sunday.

days.name: Shaheed Dibas and International Mother Language Day
days.reason: Mourning for the language movement martyrs of 1952. The day begins at midnight with a barefoot procession.

days.name: Martyrs' Day, Sahid Diwas
days.reason: A national day of mourning in Nepal, on 16 Magh in the Bikram Sambat calendar.

days.name: Remembrance observances in Sri Lanka
days.reason: Sri Lanka observes remembrance days in May that are sensitive across communities. Dates unverified.

days.name: Ching Ming and Chung Yeung
days.reason: Grave-sweeping days. Families remember their dead. Quiet, not celebratory.

days.name: Ramadan
days.reason: Not a mourning period, and not a quiet day in the strict sense. It is a restraint window: no food or feasting imagery, no daytime celebration framing, no offer that trades on urgency. The 2026 start is the date the Government of Pakistan named as 1 Ramadan 1447 for the Zakat deduction, subject to the moon.

exam_season_hints.note: Timing guidance for the marketing and lifecycle engine, and for Wobo's own tone. During an exam window Wobo does not celebrate, does not run share loops, and does not start a new course unprompted. Board-by-board dates live in school-calendar.json. Anything null there is null here, and each confidence here is the weakest confidence among the rows it summarises, never stronger.

festivals.name: New Year's Day

greeting_style.example: Happy new year, {name}. I am glad we get another year of this.
greeting_style.note: Warm, not grand. No resolutions talk, no goal setting, no year-in-review upsell.

festivals.notes: A restricted holiday in Indian central government offices, a bank holiday in Pakistan, a public holiday almost everywhere else.

festivals.name: Hazrat Ali's birthday

greeting_style.example: Warm wishes on Hazrat Ali's birthday, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Observed mainly by Shia families. Greet only where the learner has told us.

festivals.notes: Falls twice in the 2026 Gregorian year because 13 Rajab occurs in January and again in December.

festivals.name: Lohri

greeting_style.example: Happy Lohri, {name}. I hope the fire is warm and the peanuts hold out.
greeting_style.note: Playful is right for Lohri. Still no exclamation marks.

festivals.notes: Not on the central government list. Fixed by convention on 13 January, occasionally 14 January. Verify against a Punjab state holiday notification before using it in an outbound message.

festivals.name: Makar Sankranti

greeting_style.example: Happy Makar Sankranti, {name}. May your kite stay up longer than everyone else's.
greeting_style.note: In Gujarat the kite is the whole festival. In Assam it is the feast. Let the region choose the image.

festivals.notes: Listed as Makar Sankranti and Magha Bihu on the central government restricted-holiday list in both years.

festivals.name: Pongal

greeting_style.example: Happy Pongal, {name}. I hope the pot boils over exactly the way it should.
greeting_style.note: The pot boiling over is the good omen. Use it, do not explain it.

festivals.notes: Four days: Bhogi, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal, Kaanum Pongal. The central government list names only the first day. The end dates here are that first day plus three, which is the standard span; treat the later days as derived. Sri Lanka's Thai Pongal date is unverified, see the Sri Lanka gaps note.

festivals.name: Guru Gobind Singh's birthday

greeting_style.example: Wishing you a peaceful Prakash Parv, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Reverent rather than festive.

festivals.notes: Not on the 2026 central government restricted list, so 2026 is null here. Do not fill it from a panchang without a state notification.

festivals.name: Republic Day

greeting_style.example: Happy Republic Day, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Short. Civic days do not need warmth turned up.

festivals.notes: A gazetted national holiday. Schools hold flag hoisting in the morning.

festivals.name: Vasant Panchami

greeting_style.example: Happy Saraswati Puja, {name}. A good day to be a student.
greeting_style.note: This is the one festival that belongs to learning. Wobo may say so, once, without turning it into a lesson pitch.

festivals.notes: Saraswati Puja in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha; Basant Panchami in the north. In Bengali schools children write their first letters on this day.

greeting_style.example: Warm wishes on Guru Ravidas Jayanti, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Plain and respectful.

festivals.name: Maha Shivratri

greeting_style.example: A peaceful Maha Shivratri to you, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Many families fast and stay up through the night. Keep it calm, and do not send anything late at night.

festivals.notes: Also a public holiday in Nepal, where the date is set by the Ministry of Home Affairs gazette.

greeting_style.example: Wishing you a good Shiv Jayanti, {name}.
greeting_style.note: State-scoped. Maharashtra only.

festivals.name: Holika Dahan

greeting_style.example: Happy Holika Dahan, {name}. The colours come tomorrow.
greeting_style.note: The bonfire night before Holi.

festivals.notes: The central list pairs Holika Dahan with Dolyatra on the same day.

festivals.name: Holi

greeting_style.example: Happy Holi, {name}. I hope you get someone before they get you.
greeting_style.note: Holi is the one day the voice can be mischievous. Still no emoji, still no exclamation marks.

festivals.notes: A gazetted holiday in India in both years. An optional holiday in Pakistan, where the Cabinet Division lists Dulhandi on 3 March 2026 and Holi on 4 March 2026. Diaspora communities in the UK, US, Canada, Australia and the UAE celebrate on the nearest weekend, which is not modelled here.

festivals.name: Chaitra Sukladi, Ugadi, Gudi Padwa and Cheti Chand

greeting_style.example: Happy Ugadi, {name}. A new year, and the neem with the jaggery.
greeting_style.note: Use the learner's own regional name for the day. Ugadi in the Telugu and Kannada south, Gudi Padwa in Maharashtra, Cheti Chand for Sindhi families.

festivals.notes: The same lunar day carries a different name in each region. It also opens Chaitra Navratri.

festivals.name: Nowruz

greeting_style.example: Navroz Mubarak, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Two words is enough. It is the customary greeting.

festivals.notes: Falls on the March equinox as reckoned in Tehran, which can be 20 or 21 March. Not on the Indian central government list. Left null rather than guessed. The Parsi Shahenshahi new year, which most Indian Parsi families keep, is a separate entry, parsi-new-year.

greeting_style.example: Wishing you a blessed Jamat-ul-Vida, {name}.
greeting_style.note: The last Friday of Ramadan. Restrained, and no food imagery.

festivals.name: Eid al-Fitr

greeting_style.example: Eid Mubarak, {name}. I hope the house is full today.
greeting_style.note: Eid Mubarak is the greeting; do not translate it. In Singapore and Malaysia use Selamat Hari Raya. Never send it before the moon is confirmed.

festivals.notes: Every Islamic date here is subject to moon sighting. India's central government reserves the right to move Id-ul-Fitr, Id-ul-Zuha, Muharram and Id-e-Milad at short notice on the sighting; the UAE dates are Cabinet-set with a fourth day added if Ramadan runs thirty days; Pakistan's are marked in the Cabinet circular as anticipated and subject to the appearance of the moon. Wobo must never send an Eid greeting on a scheduled date alone. It waits for a same-day confirmation flag.

festivals.name: Ram Navami

greeting_style.example: Happy Ram Navami, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Plain.

festivals.notes: Closes Chaitra Navratri.

festivals.name: Mahavir Jayanti

greeting_style.example: Wishing you a peaceful Mahavir Jayanti, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Quiet in tone. Jain observance is reflective, not festive.

festivals.notes: A gazetted holiday in India.

festivals.name: Good Friday

greeting_style.note: There is no greeting for Good Friday. It is solemn. Wobo sends nothing and waits for Easter.

festivals.notes: Confirmed identically by the UK, India, Singapore, Hong Kong and Pakistan lists for both years. Not a US federal holiday.

festivals.name: Easter

greeting_style.example: Happy Easter, {name}. I hope it is a slow, good day.
greeting_style.note: Gentle. Not a party greeting.

2026.label: Family Day
2026.note: The Easter greeting goes on the Sunday. The Monday is a day off.

festivals.notes: Easter Sunday then Easter Monday. Easter Monday is a bank holiday in England, Wales and Northern Ireland but not in Scotland. South Africa calls the Monday Family Day. Hong Kong keeps the Saturday after Good Friday as well.

festivals.name: Vaisakhi, Vishu, Puthandu and Bohag Bihu

greeting_style.example: Happy Vishu, {name}. I hope the first thing you saw this morning was a good one.
greeting_style.note: Name the day the way the learner's family does. Vaisakhi in Punjab, Vishu in Kerala with the Vishukkani, Puthandu in Tamil Nadu, Bihu in Assam.

2026.label: Vaisakhi, Vishu, Meshadi, Tamil New Year
2026.note: Name the day the way the family does. The fallback greeting is the Kerala one.

2026.label: Vaisakhadi in Bengal, Bohag Bihu in Assam
2026.greeting: Happy Bohag Bihu, {name}. I hope the new year opens gently.
2026.note: Poila Boishakh in Bengal and Bohag Bihu in Assam. This is not Vishu.

2027.label: Vaisakhi, Vishu, Meshadi, Tamil New Year
2027.note: Name the day the way the family does. The fallback greeting is the Kerala one.

2027.label: Vaisakhadi in Bengal, Bohag Bihu in Assam
2027.greeting: Happy Bohag Bihu, {name}. I hope the new year opens gently.
2027.note: Poila Boishakh in Bengal and Bohag Bihu in Assam. This is not Vishu.

festivals.notes: One solar moment, many names. Sri Lanka's Sinhala and Tamil New Year falls in the same window on 13 and 14 April, but the Sri Lankan dates are unverified here. Nepal's new year, 1 Baishakh 2083, fell on 14 April 2026.

festivals.name: Pohela Boishakh

greeting_style.example: Shubho Noboborsho, {name}.
greeting_style.note: The Bengali greeting is the right one. Do not translate it.

festivals.notes: Bangladesh fixes 1 Boishakh to 14 April by the revised Bangla Academy calendar, while West Bengal keeps the traditional reckoning, which is why the Indian date is 15 April in both years. The Bangladeshi date is left null until the Ministry of Public Administration list is read.

greeting_style.example: Happy Rabindra Jayanti, {name}.
greeting_style.note: A literary day. Schools in Bengal hold recitations.

festivals.name: Buddha Purnima and Vesak

greeting_style.example: A peaceful Vesak to you, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Calm and still. Vesak is not a party.

festivals.notes: The reckonings genuinely differ. India and Singapore agree in 2027 on 20 May but not in 2026, where India keeps 1 May and Singapore 31 May. Hong Kong's official list gives the day following Buddha's Birthday as the 2026 holiday because 24 May is a Sunday; the festival day itself is derived as 24 May. Sri Lanka's Vesak Poya is left null because secondary reports conflicted and the gazette could not be read. Never assume one date across countries.

festivals.name: Eid al-Adha

greeting_style.example: Eid Mubarak, {name}. I hope the day is generous to you.
greeting_style.note: Same greeting as Eid al-Fitr. In Singapore and Malaysia, Selamat Hari Raya Haji. Arafah Day, the day before, is for standing and prayer, so send nothing then.

2026.label: Arafah Day
2026.note: Arafah Day is for standing and prayer. Nothing is sent. The Eid greeting goes on the entry below.

festivals.notes: Moon-sighting rules identical to Eid al-Fitr. The Pakistan Cabinet circular marks 27 to 29 May 2026 as 10 Zil Haj 1447 and the two days after.

festivals.name: Islamic new year

greeting_style.example: A blessed new year to you, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Muted. The Hijri new year opens the month of Muharram, which turns to mourning within days. No celebration language.

festivals.notes: Derived, not read from a list: 1 Muharram is nine days before the day of Ashura, which the Indian central government fixes at 26 June 2026 and 16 June 2027. A UAE public holiday under Cabinet Resolution No. 27 of 2024, subject to moon sighting. Not a public holiday in India.

festivals.name: Muharram, the day of Ashura

greeting_style.note: There is no greeting. Ashura is mourning. Wobo sends nothing, and if the learner mentions it, Wobo answers plainly and does not wish them well.

festivals.notes: India and Pakistan differ by a day or two because each follows its own sighting. Both are official.

greeting_style.example: Happy Rath Yatra, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Odisha above all.

festivals.name: Parsi new year

greeting_style.example: Navroz Mubarak, {name}.
greeting_style.note: The customary greeting, unchanged.

festivals.notes: The Shahenshahi reckoning most Indian Parsi families keep, which drifts and currently sits in August. Distinct from Jamshedi Navroz at the March equinox.

festivals.name: Independence Day

greeting_style.example: Happy Independence Day, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Short.

festivals.notes: In 2027 it coincides with Milad-un-Nabi and with the Parsi new year on the central list.

festivals.name: Milad-un-Nabi

greeting_style.example: Wishing you a blessed Milad-un-Nabi, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Reverent, not festive. Observance varies widely between communities, so greet only where the learner has told us.

festivals.notes: Three countries, three dates in 2026, all official. Always use the learner's country.

festivals.name: Onam

greeting_style.example: Happy Onam, {name}. I hope the sadya is enormous.
greeting_style.note: Onam belongs to Malayali families wherever they live, which for Wobo means Kerala, the Gulf and Singapore too.

festivals.notes: The central list names Thiru Onam, the main day. Kerala schools close for roughly a week around it; the state holiday list, not this file, has that window.

greeting_style.example: Happy Raksha Bandhan, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Never assume the learner has a sibling. Keep the wish about the day, not about a brother or a sister.

festivals.name: Janmashtami

greeting_style.example: Happy Janmashtami, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Families fast until midnight. Nothing after nine in the evening.

festivals.notes: Listed as Janmashtami (Vaishnava) on the central government list.

festivals.name: Ganesh Chaturthi

greeting_style.example: Happy Ganesh Chaturthi, {name}. Ganpati bappa morya.
greeting_style.note: The Marathi phrase is the whole greeting for Maharashtra families. Use it there and nowhere else.

festivals.notes: The festival runs ten days to Anant Chaturdashi. Only the first day is on the central list.

festivals.name: Navratri, Durga Puja and Dussehra

greeting_style.example: Shubho Bijoya, {name}. I hope the week was as good as it looked.
greeting_style.note: The greeting changes completely by region. Shubho Sharodiya at the start and Shubho Bijoya at the end for Bengali families; happy Navratri and happy garba in Gujarat; happy Dasara in Karnataka and the south; happy Dussehra in the north. Never send the Bengali one to a Gujarati family.

2026.label: Saptami
2026.greeting: Shubho Sharodiya, {name}. I hope the pandals are worth the queue.

2026.label: Maha Ashtami
2026.note: Recorded so the break is known. The wish goes on Saptami and again on Dashami, not on the days between.

2027.label: Saptami
2027.greeting: Shubho Sharodiya, {name}. I hope the pandals are worth the queue.

2027.label: Maha Ashtami
2027.note: Recorded so the break is known. The wish goes on Saptami and again on Dashami, not on the days between.

2027.label: Maha Navami
2027.note: Recorded so the break is known. The wish goes on Saptami and again on Dashami, not on the days between.

festivals.notes: Only the days the central government fixes are recorded. The nine nights of Navratri begin about a week before Saptami, but the first day is not on the list and is deliberately not computed here. In 2026 the government put Maha Navami and Dussehra on the same day, 20 October; in 2027 they fall on consecutive days. This is the longest school break of the autumn in eastern and northern India.

greeting_style.example: Wishing you a good Gandhi Jayanti, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Sober. It is a birthday, but a national one. Distinct from Martyrs' Day on 30 January, which is a quiet day.

greeting_style.example: Warm wishes on Valmiki Jayanti, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Plain.

festivals.name: Karwa Chauth

greeting_style.note: An adults' fast. Wobo does not greet a school-age learner for it. It is here so the calendar knows the household will be busy in the evening and so nothing lands at moonrise.

festivals.notes: Kept in the calendar for scheduling, not for greeting.

festivals.name: Diwali

greeting_style.example: Happy Diwali, {name}. I hope the house is full of light tonight.
greeting_style.note: The biggest greeting of the year for most of our learners. One line, warm, and nothing attached to it. For Sikh families the day is Bandi Chhor Divas; name it that way where we know.

festivals.notes: The 2026 memorandum notes that Diwali falls on Sunday 8 November 2026 and that some states observe Naraka Chaturdasi instead. Singapore and India diverge by a day in 2027. Diwali is a school holiday across northern and western India for roughly a week, and a single day in most other countries.

festivals.name: Naraka Chaturdasi

greeting_style.example: Happy Naraka Chaturdasi, {name}.
greeting_style.note: In the south this, not the next day, is the main Deepavali. Follow the learner's state.

2026.note: 8 November 2026 is Diwali as well. One greeting only, and Diwali carries it.

festivals.notes: The 2026 list places Naraka Chaturdasi and Diwali on the same date, 8 November, and paragraph 6 of the memorandum explains that states may take the Diwali holiday on Naraka Chaturdasi day instead.

greeting_style.example: Happy Govardhan Puja, {name}.
greeting_style.note: For Gujarati families this day is also the new year. Say Saal Mubarak where we know that.

festivals.name: Bhai Dooj

greeting_style.example: Happy Bhai Dooj, {name}.
greeting_style.note: As with Rakhi, never assume a sibling.

festivals.notes: Called Bhai Tika in Nepal, where it closes Tihar.

festivals.name: Chhath Puja

greeting_style.example: Happy Chhath, {name}. I hope the river is calm at sunrise.
greeting_style.note: A four-day fast ending at sunrise. Nothing before dawn and nothing at dusk on the offering days.

festivals.notes: The central list names the Shashthi day. The observance runs two days either side of it.

festivals.name: Guru Nanak's birthday

greeting_style.example: Happy Gurpurab, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Gurpurab is what families say. Use it.

festivals.notes: A gazetted holiday in India. An optional holiday in Pakistan, where Nankana Sahib draws pilgrims. In 2026 it falls on 24 November, the same day as Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom, which is a quiet day. The precedence rule in quiet_days settles it: the Gurpurab greeting is sent and nothing else is.

festivals.name: Christmas

greeting_style.example: Happy Christmas, {name}. I hope the day is a slow one.
greeting_style.note: Say happy Christmas, not merry, to keep the voice consistent. Christmas Eve matters more than Christmas Day in Goa, Kerala and much of Latin Christian practice.

2026.label: Christmas Eve, a restricted holiday
2026.note: Recorded because Indian offices and many schools keep it. The greeting goes on 25 December.

2027.label: Christmas Eve, a restricted holiday
2027.note: Recorded because Indian offices and many schools keep it. The greeting goes on 25 December.

2027.label: The first weekday after Christmas Day, a general holiday
2027.note: A substitute day off. The greeting went on 25 December.

festivals.notes: Christmas Eve is a restricted holiday in India. Boxing Day, 26 December, is a bank holiday in the UK, Canada, Australia, Hong Kong and South Africa, where it is the Day of Goodwill, and a Christian community holiday in Pakistan. In 2027 the UK moves both Christmas and Boxing Day to Monday 27 and Tuesday 28 December, and the US observes Christmas on Friday 24 December.

festivals.name: Lunar new year

greeting_style.example: Happy lunar new year, {name}. I hope the year is a kind one.
greeting_style.note: Gong hei fat choy in Cantonese Hong Kong, gong xi fa cai in Mandarin. Use the family's own language where we know it, and say lunar new year rather than Chinese new year when the learner is Korean or Vietnamese.

festivals.notes: Hong Kong's 2027 list substitutes the fourth day of the lunar new year for the second, which falls on a Sunday, so the official days are 6, 8 and 9 February. Singapore keeps two days in both years. The fifteen days to Chap Goh Meh matter to many families even when only the first days are holidays.

festivals.name: Ching Ming

greeting_style.note: No greeting. Families visit graves. Wobo says nothing.

festivals.notes: Hong Kong's 2026 list gazettes the day following Ching Ming, 6 April, as the general holiday because 5 April is a Sunday. The festival date is derived by subtracting one day from the gazetted holiday, the same rule as Mid-Autumn.

greeting_style.example: Happy Tuen Ng, {name}. I hope there are enough rice dumplings to go around.
greeting_style.note: The zongzi is the image everyone shares.

festivals.name: Mid-Autumn Festival

greeting_style.example: Happy Mid-Autumn, {name}. I hope you get the good mooncake.
greeting_style.note: Light and family-shaped. Lanterns and the full moon.

2026.label: holiday observed the day after, 26 September

2027.label: holiday observed the day after, 16 September

festivals.notes: Hong Kong gazettes the day following Mid-Autumn as the holiday, because the festival itself is an evening. The festival dates here are derived by subtracting one day from the gazetted holiday.

festivals.name: Chung Yeung Festival

greeting_style.note: Grave-sweeping again, and a day for the elderly. No greeting.

festivals.notes: Hong Kong's 2026 list gazettes the day following Chung Yeung, 19 October, as the general holiday because 18 October is a Sunday. The 2026 festival date is derived by subtracting one day, the same rule as Mid-Autumn and Ching Ming.

festivals.name: Rosh Hashanah

greeting_style.example: Shanah tovah, {name}.
greeting_style.note: The customary greeting. Two words, and nothing after them.

festivals.notes: Hebrew days begin at sunset the evening before, so 2026 begins at sunset on 11 September and 2027 at sunset on 1 October. Send nothing after sunset on the eve.

festivals.name: Yom Kippur

greeting_style.note: No wish. If anything is said before it, it is said on the eve, and it is not a celebration.

festivals.notes: A full fast. Nothing is sent from sunset on the eve to nightfall on the day.

festivals.name: Hanukkah

greeting_style.example: Happy Hanukkah, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Eight nights. Greet on the first, not every night.

festivals.notes: The 2026 span begins at sunset on 4 December. The 2027 dates were not read and are left null.

festivals.name: Passover

greeting_style.example: Chag sameach, {name}.
greeting_style.note: The customary greeting for the festival.

festivals.notes: The 2027 festival begins at sundown on 21 April. The 2026 dates were not read and are left null.

festivals.name: United Kingdom bank holidays

greeting_style.note: Bank holidays are days off, not occasions. Wobo does not greet them. They are here so nothing is scheduled on them and so a long weekend is recognised as one.

2026.label: Summer bank holiday, England, Wales and Northern Ireland
Battle of the Boyne, substitute day

2027.label: Summer bank holiday, England, Wales and Northern Ireland
Christmas Day and Boxing Day, substitute days

festivals.notes: Scotland does not keep Easter Monday. The May and spring bank holidays anchor the half-term breaks that matter for exam revision.

festivals.name: United States federal holidays

greeting_style.note: Wobo does not greet federal holidays. They are recorded so nothing is scheduled and so long weekends are known. Memorial Day and Patriot Day are quiet days, listed separately.

2026.label: Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr.

2027.label: Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr.

festivals.notes: The actual Independence Day is 4 July in both years; the dates above are the federal observances.

festivals.name: Thanksgiving

greeting_style.example: Happy Thanksgiving, {name}. I hope the table is loud.
greeting_style.note: The one American day worth a greeting, because it is about the household. Canada keeps its own in October.

festivals.notes: US schools close for the whole week in many districts. Canada's 2027 date was not published on the source page and is left null.

festivals.name: Halloween

greeting_style.example: Happy Halloween, {name}. I hope the costume is a good one.
greeting_style.note: Light. Children care about this one even where it is not a holiday.

festivals.notes: Not a public holiday anywhere in our list. Fixed date.

festivals.name: Canada public holidays

greeting_style.example: Happy Canada Day, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Only Canada Day earns a greeting. The rest are days off.

2026.label: Victoria Day
2026.note: Recorded as a public holiday. Not greeted.

2026.label: Saint-Jean-Baptiste Day
2026.note: Recorded as a public holiday. Not greeted.

2026.note: Recorded as a public holiday. Not greeted.

2026.note: Recorded as a public holiday. Not greeted.

2027.note: Recorded as a public holiday. Not greeted.

festivals.notes: Provinces and territories add their own. The 2027 list was not published on the source page at build time and is left null.

festivals.name: Australia public holidays

greeting_style.note: Wobo does not greet Australian public holidays. Australia Day is contested and is deliberately not greeted.

Christmas Day, Boxing Day and the additional Monday

Christmas Day, Boxing Day and the additional days

Victoria's AFL Grand Final Friday and Melbourne Cup Day, Western Australia Day, the Northern Territory Picnic Day, Canberra Day and the state Labour Days all differ and are not recorded here. Fetch the Fair Work Ombudsman list before using Australian state dates in anything outbound.

greeting_style.example: Happy Heritage Day, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Heritage Day is the one that families celebrate. Human Rights Day and the Day of Reconciliation are commemorative and are not greeted.

festivals.notes: Under the Public Holidays Act No. 36 of 1994, a public holiday falling on a Sunday moves to the Monday. That rule produced the 2026 Women's Day and 2027 Human Rights Day observances above.

greeting_style.example: Happy National Day, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Short.
Days off, not occasions. Not greeted.

festivals.name: UAE National Day

greeting_style.example: Happy National Day, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Two days, and the country decorates for a week. Greet on the first.

festivals.notes: Fixed by Cabinet Resolution No. 27 of 2024. Not transferable if it falls on a weekend.

festivals.name: Gulf national days

greeting_style.example: Happy National Day, {name}.
greeting_style.note: Name the country's own day, never a generic Gulf greeting.

festivals.notes: Fixed Gregorian national days, recorded from convention because no single official GCC list was fetched. Kuwait keeps 26 February as Liberation Day as well. Verify against each country's own government portal before anything outbound. All Islamic holidays in these countries follow the Eid, Muharram and Milad entries.

festivals.name: Dashain

greeting_style.example: Happy Dashain, {name}. I hope the tika lasts all week.
greeting_style.note: The longest holiday of the Nepali year. Schools close for two to three weeks.

2026.label: Ashoj 31 to Kartik 6, 2083
2026.note: Ashoj 2083 runs to 31 days, so Kartik 1 is 18 October and Kartik 6 is 23 October.

festivals.notes: The Ministry of Home Affairs gazette of 18 Falgun 2082 declared the Dashain holiday as Ashoj 31 to Kartik 6. The gazette itself was not retrievable, so this is reported rather than read, and the Gregorian dates are counted from the one anchor the report gives. The 2027 dates fall in the 2084 B.S. gazette, which is not yet published.

festivals.name: Tihar

greeting_style.example: Happy Tihar, {name}. I hope the lights go all the way down the street.
greeting_style.note: Five days, one for the crow, the dog, the cow, the self and the sibling.

2026.label: Kartik 22 to Kartik 26, 2083
2026.note: Counted from Kartik 1 on 18 October 2026.

festivals.notes: Same caveat as Dashain.

festivals.name: Nepali new year

greeting_style.example: Happy new year, {name}. Nayaa barsha ko shubhakamana.
greeting_style.note: The Nepali phrase is worth keeping.

festivals.notes: The Bikram Sambat year 2083 began on 14 April 2026 and ends on 13 April 2027.

festivals.name: Sri Lanka observances

greeting_style.example: Happy new year, {name}. Suba aluth avuruddak wewa.
greeting_style.note: The Sinhala and Tamil New Year in April is the big household one. Poya days are quiet and religious, not greeted.

2026.note: Fixed by statute on 4 February. Recorded from convention, because the 2026 gazette was not served. Confirm against the gazette before anything outbound.

Extraordinary Gazette No. 2438/22 of 27 May 2025 declares the 2026 public and bank holidays, including every Poya day, and it was not served at build time. Only Independence Day on 4 February, which is fixed by statute, is recorded. Read the gazette before Wobo says anything to a Sri Lankan family about a date.

festivals.name: Bangladesh national days

greeting_style.note: Shaheed Dibas on 21 February is a mourning day and is listed under quiet days, not here.
